Alex / team —

Asha — thanks for the clear asks. A few technical clarifications to help us finalize contract text:

1) BYOK / HSM: For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) we support HSM-backed keys (customer manages key material in their HSM). For Hosted, we offer an envelope-based BYOK model (you provide a wrapped key; Redwood never sees plaintext). We can accept the Exhibit B language that requires proof of separation provided the proof is defined as:
   - KMS audit logs showing key import and admin operations (ISO 8601 timestamps).
   - KMS policy documents and HSM vendor attestation (if used).

2) Access controls: We'll include an appendix table mapping roles to capabilities (KMS Admin, Key Import, Key Rotation, Escrow). Admin-level actions require two engineers + SOC approval for rotation/escrow unseal.

3) Key escrow: We do not recommend vendor-side key escrow for hosted models. If Acme requires escrow, we can accommodate as a paid add-on with documented procedures (time to restore, seals, and notarized handoff).

Proposed TOMs wording (short):
"Redwood maintains logical separation of customer key material. For hosted deployments, Redwood stores only wrapped key material. For private deployments, customer-managed HSMs hold the master key; Redwood will operate per the customer's access policy under the customer's control. Redwood will provide audit logs and HSM vendor attestations on request as specified in Exhibit B."

If that text is acceptable from legal, I can paste it into the DPA redlines doc. Otherwise I can prepare a short appendix with the exact wording we propose.

Marissa Cole
Director, Infrastructure Security
